toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% is most likely ordinary week-to-week variation. Over the previous 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354% and the policy's upper limit for a normal week is 0.482%. This week's 0.411% is inside that limit. Weeks of 0.44, 0.51 and 0.45% occurred before, were investigated, and nothing was found. The burn-rate alarm did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). The dashboard counts match the raw logs, so this isn't a counting artefact. Customers weren't affected: booking completion was flat and there were no complaints.

The finding that the v4.18 pods error at nearly twice the old rate is not evidence of a bad release. Every new pod starts with an empty cache and times out more while it warms up. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a redeploy with no code change. It adds only 10–20 errors per rollout, far less than the roughly 2,300 extra errors in the week.

Recommendation: don't roll back, and don't mute alerts. Muting the burn-rate page would remove the safety net. Note the week at ops review and apply the standard check to the following week. If next week is above 0.482%, investigate then, starting with the replica move and partner-sync timing, which I could not rule out.
